narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Chart Under Glass"**

Ballast reads the disk like a nautical chart. Free space is open water, the plain ground of every screen. The weight on the disk is drawn in five depth bands of blue: the more something weighs, the deeper its blue. What can't be moved (System Data) is buff land. Chart magenta marks only hazards the user can act on. Content tools (callouts, the dock, filter chips, the "can be cleaned safely" panel) float above the chart on Liquid Glass, while stock macOS 26 chrome (sidebar, toolbar, inspector) keeps its system glass.

The app is a native macOS SwiftUI utility built on the Storage-settings grammar: native split view, plain words, dense lists of rows. One authored moment, "drop ballast", carries the story: a cleaned item drains out of its band in the storage bar, free space counts up, and one light sweep crosses the glass. Everything else is quiet feedback. Nothing loops at idle.

Every color is defined once in `Theme` (Sources/Ballast/Views/Design/Theme.swift) for the day chart (light), the night chart (dark), and both under Increase Contrast. The frontmatter records the day chart; night and high-contrast values are in the sidecar.
keyCharacteristics: Open-water ground, depth-banded blue data, buff land, magenta for actionable hazards only.
Liquid Glass only for floating content tools; shoal surfaces for grouped rows.
One opaque ink plate per window.
Byte figures set as italic tabular soundings on one column edge.
No shadows, no borders around groups, no card-in-card.
Springs throughout, exits faster than entrances, everything off under Reduce Motion.

rules.name: The Magenta Is Hazard Rule
rules.body: Chart magenta marks only something the user can act on: low space, an item that needs a decision, a finding that needs attention. Never decoration, never a safety verdict, never an error message (errors are secondary text).

rules.name: The Heavier Is Deeper Rule
rules.body: Share bars and treemap tiles step through the depth bands by weight (`0.25 + 0.75 × fraction`). The storage bar is categorical instead: each category keeps one band between scans and through the drop (Applications `depth-4`, Your files `depth-3`, Caches `depth-2`, Build files `depth-1`, Other `depth-0`, System Data land, In Trash hatched land, Available water).

rules.name: The One Column Edge Rule
rules.body: Every byte figure is a `Sounding`, right-aligned to one tabular column edge per list (`ChartRow` fixes it at 84pt, trailing), and counts to new values with `Motion.figure`. Figures that update several times a second (live scan bytes) skip the count.

rules.name: The One Figure Rule
rules.body: Each screen has one hero figure; everything else is a sounding.

rules.name: The Space Divides Rule
rules.body: Space and headers divide content. Grouped rows sit on one shoal surface with no border, and a surface is never nested inside another.

rules.name: The No Glass On Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass is for floating content tools only, never on stock chrome (sidebar, toolbar, inspector) and never inside another glass shape. Secondary buttons inside a glass panel are `.bordered`.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Contours and outlines are one device pixel (1 / displayScale), drawn once; groups get no borders.

rules.name: The One Plate Per Window Rule
rules.body: Only the window's primary action leaves the glass as an opaque ink plate. While the Cleanup List inspector holds a ready Clean Up, every detail-column plate steps down to a shoal-blue capsule (`\.inkYields`). Sheets are their own context: their content calls `.ownsInkPlate()`, so a sheet's Done keeps its plate.

rules.name: The Control Tint Rule
rules.body: Selection controls (segmented pickers, toggle buttons) take `Theme.control`, set on each control, never the system accent and never a scene-wide tint. Links stay in the system link color.

rules.name: The Shape First Rule
rules.body: A verdict is a shape before it is a color: safe is a checkmark circle, quit first a pause rectangle, caution a triangle, protected a lock. Color (green, sea, amber, slate) is the second cue and never magenta.

dos: **Do** keep one ink plate per window: the primary action only, stepping down via `\.inkYields` while the Cleanup List holds a ready Clean Up.
**Do** set `.tint(Theme.control)` on each segmented picker and toggle button, never the system accent; put `.ownsInkPlate()` on every sheet's content.
**Do** set every byte figure as a `Sounding` on one trailing column edge per list.
**Do** give every verdict its `SafetyMark` shape; color is only the second cue.
**Do** keep each storage category in its own band; step share bars and treemap tiles through the bands by weight.
**Do** route every animation through `Motion` so Reduce Motion turns it off.
**Do** use `ChartSection` for grouped rows and `EmptyChart` for empty or all-clear states.
donts: **Don't** use chart magenta for decoration, safety verdicts or plain errors.
**Don't** put glass on glass, or glass on the sidebar, toolbar or inspector.
**Don't** set the control tint scene-wide; it fills every glass and bordered button.
**Don't** add shadows, borders around groups, or a surface inside a surface.
**Don't** run idle loops; motion without input is allowed only while data is loading.
**Don't** add a second hero figure to a screen.
